Die Dokumentation dieser Integration wird von ihrem Autor geschrieben und ist bisher nur auf Englisch verfügbar.

Brings the [TRMNL](https://trmnl.com) e-ink displays of your account into
Gladys, through the official TRMNL account API: battery, Wi-Fi and sleep mode
of each display.

> **Never tested with a real device.** This integration was written from the
> `trmnl` Python client (the one of the Home Assistant integration) and
> tested against a simulated TRMNL API only. Unofficial, not affiliated with
> TRMNL.

## What you get

One device per display (Discovery tab), keyed by its TRMNL id:

- **Battery** (%), and **battery voltage** (V);
- **Wi-Fi strength** (0 to 100, as TRMNL rates it) and **Wi-Fi signal**
  (dBm);
- **Sleep mode** (on or off) and **sleep hours** (for example
  `22:00-08:00`, in the time zone of your TRMNL account);
- as an option, two **buttons**: "Turn the sleep mode on" and "Turn the
  sleep mode off" (see below).

What the screen shows (playlists, plugins) stays managed in TRMNL. The API
gives no "last contact" time of a display: it is not shown.

## Getting started

1. On [trmnl.com](https://trmnl.com), open **Account** and copy the **API
   key** of your account (it starts with `user_`).
2. In Gladys, open this integration, paste the key and save. The key is kept
   by Gladys in its database, never shown again, and sent only to trmnl.com,
   in the `Authorization` header of the requests.
3. Your displays appear in the Discovery tab: create the ones you want.

## How often it reads

- One request for all the displays, every refresh interval (15 minutes by
  default, from 5 minutes to 1 hour). A display reports its battery and
  signal when it wakes up: reading more often rarely shows more.
- **Never faster than the interval**: neither Gladys reconnecting, nor a
  configuration saved unchanged, nor the Discovery button, nor "Test the
  connection", nor a restart of the container (the time of the last attempt
  is kept) adds a reading. A new key is tried one minute at most after the
  last attempt.
- After an error, a new try after the interval, then twice that, up to
  1 hour.
- 429 (TRMNL asks to slow down) or 5xx: a pause of what TRMNL asks, else 15
  or 5 minutes, between 1 minute and 6 hours, kept across restarts. No
  reading and no command during the pause.
- **Key refused** (401): no automatic try any more, restarts included. Paste
  a new key (generated again on trmnl.com; saving the same key again does
  nothing), or press "Test the connection" once the interval has passed: the
  refusal is erased only by a successful reading. A 403 (it may come from the
  network protecting trmnl.com) is not a refusal of the key: tried again like
  any other error.
- After a restart that follows a successful reading, the integration shows
  "connected" at once, until the next reading.

## Sleep mode buttons (off by default)

Tick "Allow changing the sleep mode of the displays" in the configuration.
Each display then gets two buttons (never a switch: no voice assistant nor
"turn everything off" can reach them). Each press:

1. reads the display from TRMNL again (and checks it is the same display:
   MAC address and friendly id); when it already is in the mode asked,
   nothing is sent;
2. checks again that the option is still ticked, then changes the sleep
   mode;
3. reads the display back: the command is said done only when TRMNL shows
   the new value. Otherwise: "Command sent, without confirmation" (the next
   reading shows the real mode).

Nothing is sent later than 3.5 seconds after the press (Gladys waits 5
seconds), nor during a 429/5xx pause; 6 commands per minute at most.

## Questions to testers

If you own a TRMNL display, tell us (forum, or a GitHub issue): do the
battery, voltage and signal match what trmnl.com shows? Do the sleep mode
buttons act on the display?

## Data and privacy

The integration only talks to trmnl.com. It keeps in its `/data` volume: a
random key, the fingerprint (HMAC) of a refused key (erased at the first
success; never a fingerprint of a key that works), the end of a pause, the
time of the last attempt, and the list of displays (id, name, friendly id,
MAC address). It does not read your profile (name, e-mail).

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt TRMNL in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your TRMNL account | `section` | Nein | Brings the TRMNL e-ink displays of your account into Gladys, through the official TRMNL account API (trmnl.com) and the API key of your account: for each display its battery (charge and voltage), its Wi-Fi strength and signal, its sleep mode and sleep hours. Read every refresh interval, never faster. Optional buttons turn the sleep mode on or off (off by default, see below). What the screen shows (playlists, plugins) stays in TRMNL. Never tested with a real device. Unofficial, not affiliated with TRMNL. |
| API key of your account | `secret` | Ja | On trmnl.com, Account, the "API key" of your account (it starts with user_). Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to trmnl.com, in the Authorization header of the requests. |
| Refresh | `select` | Ja | How often Gladys reads TRMNL (one request for all the displays). A display reports its battery and signal when it wakes up, often every 15 minutes: reading more often rarely shows more. |
| Language of the names | `select` | Nein | Used for the names of the features added from now on. |
| Sleep mode buttons | `section` | Nein | By default Gladys only reads. Once allowed below, each display gets two buttons, "Turn the sleep mode on" and "Turn the sleep mode off" (never a switch: no voice assistant nor "turn everything off" can reach them). Each press reads the display first, changes its sleep mode in your TRMNL account, then reads it back: it is said done only when TRMNL shows the new value. |
| Allow changing the sleep mode of the displays | `boolean` | Nein |  |

## So installierst du TRMNL in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: TRMNL erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-trmnl:0.1.2`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-trmnl](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-trmnl).

TRMNL benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

TRMNL ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
